                    ### Question
                    A group of scientists is conducting an experiment on the human cells involved in the immune response. They genetically modify B cells so they do not express the cluster of differentiation 21 (CD21) on their cell surfaces. The pathogenesis of which of the following organisms would most likely be affected by this genetic modification?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)
opb. Measles virus
opc. Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)
opd. Human papillomavirus
ope. Parvovirus B19

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Genetic modification of B cells to not express CD21 would most likely affect the pathogenesis of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and Measles virus. CD21 is important for the entry of both EBV and Measles virus into B cells. HIV, Human papillomavirus (HPV), and Parvovirus B19 pathogenesis are not directly affected by the absence of CD21 on B cells.
